summary: Standardize Instrument Comprehension (IC) beginner JSONs to use the generator pattern, instrument_panel uiSpec, and image-based answer choices consistent with AFOQT/Trivium style.

context.problem: Earlier Instrument Comprehension prototypes had poorly defined instruments and non-standard UI specs. Some versions rendered text-only choices or used vague 'replace with jet image' placeholders without a consistent data structure for attitude/heading and choice images.
context.desiredOutcome: All beginner IC questions are generated from a simple profile list (bank, pitch, heading, view, spriteId) through a Node generator, outputting standardized JSON. The uiSpec uses instrument_panel with artificialHorizon and compass data, and choices A–D are always image-based, with A constructed as the only correct combination.

linkedPatches.note: Patch 20 established generator-style/meta-style thinking and shared UI contracts for Table Reading. Patch 21 mirrors that approach for Instrument Comprehension.

logic: choiceSprites.A must EXACTLY match artificialHorizon.bankDegrees, artificialHorizon.pitchDegrees, and compass.headingDegrees.
choiceSprites.B must differ only in headingDegrees (wrong heading, same bank/pitch as A).
choiceSprites.C must differ only in bankDegrees (wrong bank side or magnitude, same heading/pitch as A).
choiceSprites.D must differ only in pitchDegrees (wrong climb/dive, same heading/bank as A).

choicesContract.note: Renderer uses choiceSprites[A–D] to resolve specific images; JSON only stores logical data and spriteIds.

question.answerRule: For generator-based IC beginner questions, answer must be 'A' by construction.

contentStyle.questionTemplate: Which airplane best matches the instruments (DESCRIPTION)?
contentStyle.copilotInstructionTemplate: Render an attitude indicator and heading indicator matching DESCRIPTION. Use choiceSprites A–D as jet silhouettes; only A should exactly match bank, pitch, and heading.
contentStyle.explanationFocus: Explain that the correct choice is the only one matching all three: bank, pitch, and heading.
stepsC1: 1. Read the bank from the attitude indicator (which wing is lower).
2. Read the pitch from the horizon (nose above, level, or below).
3. Read the heading from the compass card.
4. Compare each airplane silhouette to these three instrument readings.
5. Eliminate any choice that disagrees on bank, pitch, or heading; select the one that matches all three.
contentStyle.fastStrategy: Match heading first to eliminate obviously wrong jets, then check bank direction and pitch.

fields.bankDegrees: number; positive = right bank, negative = left bank, 0 = level
fields.pitchDegrees: number; positive = climb, negative = descent, 0 = level
fields.correctSpriteId: string; base name of the correct jet sprite (e.g., 'jet_front_bank_right_north')
fields.description: string; human-readable description used in question text

example.description: climbing right turn toward the northeast

scriptBehavior: 1. Read a profiles array describing each question’s correct attitude and heading.
2. For each profile, build uiSpec.instrument_panel with artificialHorizon, compass, and choiceSprites A–D using the distractor rules.
3. Inject question, copilotInstruction, choices, answer, explanation, steps, and fastStrategy following the schemaRules.question.contentStyle.
4. Wrap questions in a top-level object with subjectId, subtopicId, difficulty, part, and questions[].
5. Print JSON to stdout for redirection into the *_partX.json files.

uiInstructions.purpose: Describe how to render instrument_panel uiSpec and image choices to match AFOQT/Trivium style.
requirements: Attitude indicator must display bank (roll) and pitch using a horizon line and aircraft symbol.
Compass/heading indicator must display headingDegrees numerically and/or graphically.
Choices A–D must be rendered as four separate aircraft images sourced from spriteIds in choiceSprites.
The question stem and instruments appear on top/left; four jet images are presented as selectable answers beneath or beside, matching Trivium AFOQT and pamphlet layout patterns.
The renderer must treat choice text values ('IMAGE') as non-informational placeholders; actual information comes from choiceSprites.

migrationSteps.title: Create or confirm generator meta
details: Ensure instrument_comprehension_generator_meta.json exists and matches the generatorRules and schemaRules in this patch.
If older ad-hoc IC JSONs exist, mark them as deprecated or move them to a legacy/ folder.

migrationSteps.title: Implement generator scripts
details: Create generate_ic_beginner_part1.js using the profile-driven generator pattern.
Populate profiles with at least 25 entries covering a variety of simple beginner attitudes.
Repeat for generate_ic_beginner_part2.js and instrument_comprehension_beginner_part2.json with ids ic_b1_026–ic_b1_050.

migrationSteps.title: Align existing JSONs
details: If beginner IC JSONs already exist, regenerate them using the new generator instead of editing them manually.
- id matches the expected sequence and pattern.
- B, C, D each violate exactly ONE of heading, bank, or pitch.

migrationSteps.title: Wire UI instructions to frontend
details: Confirm the frontend IC component reads uiSpec.instrument_panel and choiceSprites.
Ensure instrument_comprehension_ui_instructions.json is used as the contract for layout and styling.
Verify that four aircraft images render correctly, with the instruments above and the jets below, visually similar to Trivium-style AFOQT examples.

acceptanceCriteria: 1. instrument_comprehension_beginner_part1.json and instrument_comprehension_beginner_part2.json are both generated by scripts, not hand-edited.
2. Each beginner IC question contains a valid instrument_panel uiSpec with artificialHorizon, compass, and choiceSprites A–D.
3. Choice A is always the only fully correct jet; B/C/D differ by exactly one parameter each (heading, bank, or pitch).
4. Choice text entries are all 'IMAGE'; actual visual differences are driven by choiceSprites and spriteIds.
5. The IC UI renders attitude + heading instruments and four image choices in a layout that matches AFOQT-style instrument comprehension questions.
6. All IC beginner questions conform to the generator meta spec and the C1 + fastStrategy explanation patterns used in the rest of the AFOQT project.
